issues.display_title: Issue #79: Migrate existing local files to MinIO (one-shot SSE endpoint)
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Description

Add a temporary, auth-gated endpoint POST /v1/admin/migrate-storage that walks STORAGE_PATH and uploads every file to MinIO with its relative path as the object key (1:1 with the MinIO integration key scheme). Streams per-file progress as SSE (OK {key} / FAIL {key}: {err} / final done ok=N fail=N), reusing the SSE pattern from predict.go. Idempotent — re-running only overwrites identical keys, so a second pass picks up any delta written during cutover.

Why

Files uploaded before the MinIO integration exist only on local disk and must be preserved.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Endpoint requires authentication; unauthorized requests get 401/403
  • Every file under STORAGE_PATH appears in mapthru with the correct key
  • Progress streamed per file; non-zero failures clearly reported in the final summary
  • Re-running the endpoint is safe (idempotent)
  • Post-migration verification documented: object count matches local file count + spot-check via file GET API
  • Cleanup: endpoint route + handler deleted after cutover; local disk removed only after verification

Dependencies

Depends on #78

issues.display_title: Issue #80: Harden upload file validation
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Description

Upload validation currently trusts the client-supplied Content-Type multipart header and takes the file extension from the client filename. Replace with server-side checks: sniff actual content via http.DetectContentType (stdlib) on the first 512 bytes, and derive the stored extension from the validated MIME type (map already exists in shared.go) instead of filepath.Ext(filename). Decide SVG policy: drop image/svg+xml from the allowlist, or keep accepting it but serve with Content-Disposition: attachment to neutralize stored-XSS via inline SVG script.

Why

A file that merely claims to be an image passes today's checks. SVG served inline as image/svg+xml can execute script in the user's session (stored XSS).

Acceptance Criteria

  • Genuine PNG/JPEG/WebP uploads succeed
  • A non-image file with a spoofed Content-Type: image/png header is rejected with 400
  • Stored extension always matches detected MIME, regardless of client filename
  • SVG either rejected, or never rendered inline from the file GET endpoint
  • Applies to both project-file upload and avatar upload paths

Dependencies

Depends on #78 (touches same files; do after to avoid rebase pain)

issues.display_title: Issue #81: Strip server internals from upload responses
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Description

Upload success and error responses expose server internals: storagePath (absolute storage root) in ProjectUpload's 201 body, and storage_path in error bodies of project_upload.go and update_profile.go. Remove them. Clients only need relativePath, fileName, fileUrl, fileSize, fileType.

Why

Absolute filesystem layout is reconnaissance data for an attacker and useless to the FE (a matching FE task switches it to relativePath).

Acceptance Criteria

  • 201 response contains no absolute paths (storagePath removed)
  • Error responses contain no storage_path
  • FE upload, wizard flow, and AI generate still work (coordinate with FE task to consume relativePath)

Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Description

Replace local-disk file storage with MinIO (endpoint 192.168.1.12:9199, bucket mapthru). Initialize a single *minio.Client in config alongside config.DB, configured from env: MINIO_ENDPOINT, MINIO_ACCESS_KEY, MINIO_SECRET_KEY, MINIO_BUCKET, MINIO_USE_SSL. Why

Files currently live on the app server's disk: they don't survive server replacement, can't be shared across instances, and fill local storage.

Scope of change

  • src/action/v1/predict/predict.go — os.ReadFile -> GetObject; replace path-prefix validation with object-key validation
  • src/action/v1/auth/avatar.go, src/action/v1/auth/update_profile.go — same swap for avatars
  • src/action/v1/shared/shared.go — retire StoragePath() / ResolvePath() once all callers are migrated

Acceptance Criteria

  • Upload stores the object in bucket mapthru, nothing written to local disk
  • File GET, delete, avatar upload/serve, and AI predict flow work unchanged from the FE
  • No MinIO credentials hardcoded or logged; config from env only

  • Build + tests green

Overview

  • Draft or unpublished project with viewer, editor, or owner role: 200.

issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 24/07/26

✅ Implementation: Invite Unregistered Emails (Task #105 / PR #113 )

Overview

members/Create used to return 404 "no user with that email" when a project
owner invited someone who had not signed up yet — a dead end. This task replaces
that 404 with a persistent invitation that is claimed automatically the moment
the invited email creates an account (email or Google), joining them to the
project with the role they were invited at.

Code Implementation

  1. project_invitations table (src/models/models.go):

    • New ProjectInvitation model (id, project_id, email lowercase, role,
      invited_by, claimed_at nullable, timestamps) with a unique index on
      (project_id, email). Mirrors the ProjectMember pattern: manual
      ID/timestamps, BeforeCreate UUID hook, no soft-delete.
    • Registered in AllModels() so GORM AutoMigrate provisions it, and backed by
      an explicit SQL migration (migrations/202607240001_add_project_invitations.sql)
      using CREATE TABLE / UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS so both paths coexist
      idempotently.

  2. Invitation branch (src/action/v1/members/create.go):

    • On gorm.ErrRecordNotFound for the target email, upsert a ProjectInvitation
      (FirstOrCreate(...).Assign(Role)) keyed on (project_id, email) — so a
      re-invite updates the pending role instead of erroring — and respond
      201 {"invited": true, "email": ...}. The existing-user path (add member +
      collaborator email) is unchanged.

  3. Claim helper (src/action/v1/members/claim.go):

    • ClaimInvitations(db, userID, email) loads every unclaimed invitation for
      the email, upserts a ProjectMember with the invited role (idempotent for a
      user who is already a member), and stamps claimed_at. It accepts a
      *gorm.DB so callers run it inside their own transaction or standalone.

  4. Claim wiring — proven ownership only (src/action/v1/auth/verifyEmail.go,
    src/action/v1/auth/google.go):

    • Email registration produces an unverified account, so claiming happens
      inside the VerifyEmail transaction — after email ownership is proven —
      rather than at register time (which would let anyone claim a victim's
      invitations by registering their email first).
    • Google verifies the email upstream, so the Google flow claims immediately on
      auto-provision, and also when it lifts a previously-unverified existing
      account to verified (see Task #113 review fix).

Testing

    claimed_at; idempotent re-claim and already-member role upsert.
  • routes/v1/role_matrix_test.go: invite-unknown returns 201 {invited:true} and
    writes a single invitation row; re-invite upserts the role.

Description

issues.display_title: Issue #117: Stamp created_at on canvas objects (server-authoritative) + backfill migration
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Backend half of FE GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#392 (editor object list must sort newest→oldest instead of grouping by type). Decided approach: Option C — server-authoritative created_at.

Context

The editor object list currently groups by type because there is no per-object creation order anywhere. FE stamps a provisional created_at (epoch ms) on each object as it is created; the backend canonicalizes it so ordering is consistent across clients and survives blob round-trips.

The canvas is stored as an opaque blob (canvas_data / the floorplan payload) — today neither the API nor the socket parses objects. This task introduces that parsing on the API side only. The socket (gothru-maps-socket) needs no change: edit.handler.ts relays an opaque snapshot string, so created_at rides inside it automatically.

Scope

  • On project save (canvas/floorplan blob write), parse the level objects per type and assign a monotonic created_at to any object lacking one, keyed by object id:
    • layout.walls[], layout.areas[]
    • floorplanMeta.doors[], floorplanMeta.windows[] (⚠️ these carry no id — key by array index within the level, or agree an id with FE)
    • shapes[], points[], safetyAnnotations[], panoramas[]
  • Never overwrite an existing created_at (FE's provisional value wins; server only fills gaps and normalizes).
  • Write the enriched blob back so the value persists.
  • Migration: backfill created_at for existing projects' blobs. Legacy objects have no historical timestamp anywhere, so order is best-effort (type-traversal); old projects can't be made exact — documented limitation, same for any approach.

Caveats to keep in mind

  • Schema coupling: the parser now depends on the FE object schema. Any new object type/field on FE must be mirrored here. Keep one shared shape doc.
  • Collab edge case: objects created during a live collab session sync via the socket without hitting an API save, so they carry only the FE-provisional created_at until the next persist. That is by design (hybrid) — the server just canonicalizes later.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Saving a project stamps created_at on every object that lacks one; existing values are untouched.
  • Objects round-trip through save/load with created_at preserved.
  • Migration backfills existing projects without corrupting blobs (dry-run/verify first).
  • go build ./... and go test ./... green (predict tests may fail on sandbox /tmp perms — pre-existing).

RESULT

Shipped in PR #118 (commit 24a9f38), merged to development.

  • shared.StampCanvasCreatedAt walks canvas_data as generic JSON (json.Decoder + UseNumber, so coordinates and ids re-encode byte-identical) over a list of known object array paths: layout.walls, layout.areas, floorplanMeta.doors, floorplanMeta.windows, shapes, points, safetyAnnotations, panoramas. Deliberately not a mirror of the FE structs — unknown/new fields round-trip untouched, and only a brand-new object array needs a line here. That keeps the FE↔BE coupling to a path list instead of a schema copy.
  • Wired into both canvas writers: project.Update and floorplan.Post.

issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 10/08/26

✅ Implementation: Global User Role and Support Authorization Guard (Task #121 / PR #129 )

Overview

This task adds a global user role for support authorization. The role is separate from project-level owner, editor, and viewer permissions.

Code Implementation

  1. Global User Role (src/models/models.go):

    • Added Role to models.User as varchar(20) with NOT NULL and an empty-string default.
    • Kept the global role independent from ProjectMember.Role.
    • Existing and unknown role values remain non-support unless they exactly equal support.

  2. Database Migration (migrations/202608100001_add_users_role.sql):

    • Adds public.users.role using ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS.
    • Uses NOT NULL DEFAULT '' so existing rows are backfilled safely and fresh/existing database schemas match.

  3. Support Authorization Middleware (src/middleware/auth.go):

    • Added middleware.SupportOnly().
    • Returns 401 Unauthorized when no authenticated user exists in the request context.
    • Allows access only when middleware.GetUser(c).Role == "support".
    • Returns 403 Forbidden for empty, unknown, non-support, or project-level role values.
    • Reads the role only from the database-backed authenticated user loaded by middleware.Auth(); no request body or JWT role is trusted.

  4. Current User Response (src/controllers/v1/auth/me.go):

    • Added role to the existing GET /v1/auth/me user response.
    • Existing response fields remain unchanged.

Testing

src/middleware/auth_test.go covers:

  • Exact support role passes.
  • Non-support role returns 403.
  • Empty role returns 403.
  • Unknown or differently-cased role returns 403.
  • Project owner role returns 403.
  • Missing authenticated user returns 401.

Security Decision

The role is deliberately excluded from JWT claims. middleware.Auth() loads the current user row on every request, so role changes and revocations take effect immediately instead of remaining valid for the session token's 30-day lifetime.

Verification

go build ./...
go vet ./...

Both commands pass. Test execution on the local Windows environment is blocked by Application Control when Go attempts to launch generated test executables; PR review verification reports the middleware and route tests passing.

PRD #120 (Support Feedback Management API). FE counterpart: GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#578.

Description

There is no global role concept in this repo. models.User (src/models/models.go:27) has no role field, and ProjectMember roles (owner/editor/viewer) are per-project only. The support inbox endpoints in #120 need a global support role plus one centralized guard.

Why

Every support endpoint (#120 sections 4–7) is gated on this. Without a single fail-closed helper, the guard gets re-implemented per route and one of them ends up wrong.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Role field on models.User — varchar(20), default empty string
  • SQL migration migrations/<ts>_add_users_role.sql adding the column (AutoMigrate covers fresh DBs; explicit SQL keeps existing CockroachDB deploys in sync — same pattern as 202607240001_add_project_invitations.sql)
  • middleware.SupportOnly() — passes only when middleware.GetUser(c).Role == "support", exact match
  • Fails closed: missing, empty, or unknown role → 403
  • Role is never read from the request body or any client-controlled input
  • Project owner/editor/viewer grants no support access
  • GET /v1/auth/me returns role (src/controllers/v1/auth/me.go) — additive, existing fields unchanged
  • Tests: support → pass, non-support → 403, empty role → 403, unknown role → 403, unauthenticated → 401, project owner → 403
  • src/routes/v1/role_matrix_test.go and existing auth/login/me tests still green

Scope decision — role stays out of the JWT

The PRD asks for the global role to be embedded in issued JWTs. Descoped deliberately, do not implement.

middleware.Auth() (src/middleware/auth.go:37-40) already loads the full user row from the database on every request, so GetUser(c).Role is available with no token change. Meanwhile SessionTokenTTL is 30 days (src/utils/jwt.go:12) — a role baked into the token would keep revoked support access alive for up to 30 days after the role is removed.

Dependencies

None. Blocks all other #120 tasks.
